narrative.overview:
Snapbooth Glass is a luminous, glass-wrapped photobooth: a compact kiosk of frosted panes, aurora glows, and crisp specular highlights that feels premium yet playful in a live event moment. The interface behaves like stacked glass set against a deep midnight scene—light drifts behind it, surfaces catch highlights, and controls invite touch without stealing attention from the camera and the keepsake strip.

The visual philosophy is playful, luminous, polished. Translucency, blur, and soft color blooms create atmosphere; confident Syne display moments and calm Figtree UI copy keep the experience legible and effortless. Density stays comfortable for quick, in-the-moment decisions (style, shoot, retake, save/share) while giving the resulting strip a sense of occasion.
keyCharacteristics: Frosted glass layering with specular rims, soft ambient lift, and aurora backlighting (never flat slabs).
Deep midnight grounds (#070b1d) animated by Electric Amethyst, Aurora Mint, Flash Magenta, and Warm Filament blooms.
Syne for expressive display/brand moments; Figtree for clear, friendly controls and body text.
Tactile pill controls and panels with visible hover/focus/pressed states and generous tap targets (≥44px).
Photo/strip content remains the hero; UI chrome frames and elevates the keepsake rather than competing with it.

rules.name: The Luminous Rarity Rule
rules.body: Aurora accents (especially Electric Amethyst, Aurora Mint, Flash Magenta) earn attention through contrast against Midnight Void and frosted glass. Use saturated accents for actions, focus, active/selected states, and ambient glow—not as large flat fills that drown the camera view or the strip.

rules.name: The Camera-First Voice Rule
rules.body: Typography frames the moment; it does not compete with the live preview or the photo strip. Reserve Syne’s weight and tight tracking for a few key moments (hero, brand, section anchors) and let Figtree carry instructions and controls.

rules.name: The Glass, Not Weight Rule
rules.body: Prefer translucency, blur, rim light, and ambient separation over heavy opaque elevation steps. Lift communicates layering; it must never muddy the camera feed or reduce text/strip contrast.

dos: Do preserve frosted glass layering: pair translucent fills (e.g. `rgba(13,19,48,0.32)` / `rgba(255,255,255,0.07)`) with `backdrop-filter: blur(...) saturate(...)`, soft ambient shadows, and specular rims/highlights as in `.glass`/`.topbar`.
Do keep the camera preview and photo strip as the visual focus; use Midnight Void (#070b1d) grounds and restrained UI chrome so captures remain clear.

Do use Syne 800 for display/brand anchors and Figtree for body/controls, maintaining the observed scale (display `clamp(2.5rem,6vw,4.1rem)/0.98`, labels 0.72–0.85rem tracked/uppercase where established).
Do use tactile pill controls (min 44px targets) with explicit hover, active, selected (`aria-pressed="true"`), and disabled states; keep `:focus-visible` highly visible with Focus Cyan (#7ff3e8).
Do apply aurora accents (Electric Amethyst #7c5cff, Aurora Mint #2ee6d6, Flash Magenta #ff5fa2, Warm Filament #ffc46b) for gradients, glows, selection, and emphasis per the Luminous Rarity Rule.
Do honor reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`) by disabling/simplifying animations, transitions, and transform effects as the current implementation does.
donts: Don't flatten the system into opaque, solid panels or remove blur/rim-light layering; depth must read as glass with ambient lift, not heavy material slabs.
Don't introduce large flat floods of saturated accent color behind the camera/stage or strip; accents should glow and highlight, not overpower content.
Don't replace Syne/Figtree with unestablished typefaces or collapse the display-vs-UI hierarchy into a single uniform text style.
Don't create controls without clear state feedback or with tap targets below 44px; avoid hover-only affordances.
Don't add heavy drop shadows, harsh borders, or busy textures that compete with the frosted/aurora material or reduce legibility on dark glass.
Don't ignore accessibility baselines: maintain WCAG 2.1 AA contrast on text/controls, visible focus, and reduced-motion support.
